1.why: All MFA routes use authenticated() and operate only on accountFor(session.userId); body fields like userId/accountId are rejected by forbiddenIdentity/csrfValid.

2.why: Identity codes are bound to the calling session’s identityHash; TOTP/recovery secrets are per-account, so the same code does not authorize a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets account.mfaEnabled and issues recovery codes; no code invalidates other existing sessions for that account.

4.why: totpSecret is stored via AES-GCM encryptValue; recovery codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes in recoveryCodes.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, recovery codes, and OTPs are produced with crypto.getRandomValues / WebCrypto.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie holds secrets, OTPs, or session tokens.

7.why: Server validates login/password shape, OTP via safeOtp, recovery via safeRecovery, JSON body size/shape, and csrf before use.

8.why: Client renders with textContent only; API returns JSON; CSP nonce disallows inline script injection.

9.why: validRedirect allow-lists only #/signin, #/identity, #/setup, #/confirmed, #/recovery and sign-in rejects other redirect values.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Generic error bodies, no stack traces to clients, secrets not placed in URLs; server comments/code avoid logging OTP seeds, backup codes, or session tokens.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use (identityUsed) and time-bound (identityExpires); TOTP steps are consumed in totpUsedSteps; recovery codes flip to used.

14.why: identityAttempts, totpAttempts, recoveryAttempts, and signInAttempts lock after MAX_FAILURES within LOCK_MS.

15.why: Sign-in destroys the old session and creates a new id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in readSession; logout calls destroySession and expires the cookie.
